title: Playing Philadelphia house rent parties at fourteen
summary: He describes rent parties as a living for the hosts, with pigs feet and potato salad, and the lack of anything but an ordinary piano.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So when I got to [be] about fourteen years old, I was able to play for the house rent parties. You know, the house rent parties in those days were not for fun. For the people giving the party was to make a living. Because they'd only charge you ten cents. Then a lot of people come into them, and then they had a side issue, they would serve say pigs feet and potato salad, and sometimes they'd have something else, but that was the most thing, was pigs feet and potato salad.

Now, we would get maybe, some time, we'd come in a party of three, because we could play because in those days there wasn't no pianola, there wasn't no radios, there wasn't no television, nothing like that. So, we had to -- the only way they could have any fun like that, where a piano was concerned, it was with, on just
an ordinary piano, that's all most poor people in those days could afford.
